title: Boron Deficiency in Plants: Signs, Causes and How to Fix It
metaTitle: Boron Deficiency in Plants: Signs and Fixes
metaDescription: Boron deficiency shows on the young leaves first. See the signs crop by crop, what causes it, and the fertilizer sold here that fixes it.
excerpt: Boron deficiency in plants starts on the young leaves and the growing tip. Boron is part of the cell walls and keeps the growing tips of shoots and roots dividing. Pollen needs it to sprout and grow, so it decides flowering, fruit set and seed set. It also helps move sugars inside the plant. Here are the signs in each crop, what brings it, how to be sure and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Coconut frond with leaflets stuck together and crumpled like an accordion: a boron shortage sign

blocks.text: Boron is immobile in the plant, so the damage shows first on the growing point and the young leaves. The growing tip can die while the older leaves still look normal.
Boron deficiency symptoms

The growing tip stops and dies, and young leaves come out thick, brittle, curled or crumpled. Stems may crack or turn hollow, as in hollow stem of cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower and cracked celery stalks. Papaya fruit grows bumpy and may ooze latex, and many crops drop flowers or set poor fruit. In rice the tips of new leaves turn white and roll, and plants may fail to make panicles.
Boron deficiency by crop

Each crop shows it its own way. So find yours in the tables below, then open its page for the photo and the full fix, like the one for [boron in rice](/nutrient-deficiencies/rice-nutrient-deficiency#boron).

blocks.text: What causes boron deficiency

Boron washes easily out of sandy soils, and the heavy rains of the wet season and typhoons leach it below the roots. Soils low in organic matter hold little, and a dry spell makes it worse, because roots stop feeding in the dry topsoil. High pH and heavily limed soils also lock it up. Papaya, cauliflower, celery, tomato, peanut and forage legumes need more boron than most crops.
How to be sure it is boron

Calcium shortage also kills growing tips and deforms young leaves, so a tissue test may be needed to tell the two apart. Hollow or cracked stems and bumpy papaya fruit point to boron, while blossom end rot points to calcium. A soil test for boron is only a rough guide, so a leaf tissue test is the better check. In papaya, leaf stalks with about 20 parts per million of boron or less go with bumpy fruit. While about 25 or more is normal.
How to fix boron deficiency

Borax (11 percent boron) or Solubor (20 percent boron) are the usual materials, broadcast and mixed well into the soil. For papaya, a typical rate is 1 to 3 kg of boron per hectare, or 0.5 to 5 grams of borax around each tree. Never put boron in the seed row, because it harms germinating seed, and let the soil test set the rate.
A typical borax spray for papaya is 0.25 percent, about 2.5 grams per liter of water. Test it on a few plants first, because boron toxicity is easy to cause.

How to keep boron deficiency away

Add compost and manure, which hold and release boron, and avoid over liming. On sandy soils and for boron hungry crops such as papaya and cauliflower, give a small dose each season instead of one big one.

blocks.title: Too much is a problem too
blocks.text: The gap between too little and too much boron is very narrow. Above about 5 parts per million of available boron in the soil, many crops yellow and burn at the leaf edges.

blocks.text: Boron deficiency questions

items.q: What does boron deficiency look like?
items.a: The growing tip dies and young leaves turn thick, brittle and curled. Stems may crack or turn hollow, flowers drop, and fruit such as papaya grows lumpy.

items.q: Why is my papaya fruit bumpy?
items.a: Bumpy, lumpy papaya fruit is a classic sign of boron shortage, often with latex oozing from the fruit. A borax spray of about 0.25 percent, or a small dose of borax around the tree, prevents it on the fruit that forms later.

items.q: How much borax should I use?
items.a: Very little, because boron turns toxic easily. A typical rate is 0.5 to 5 grams of borax around a papaya tree, and the soil or leaf test decides.

items.q: Can I mix borax into the fertilizer I put in the seed row?
items.a: No. Boron placed in the seed row harms germination, so broadcast it and work it well into the soil instead.
